::: {#def-bigram-model}

#### Bigram model

A **bigram model** is a [language model](#def-language-model) in which the distribution of each symbol depends only on the symbol before it
[@goodfellow2016deep, section 12.4.1].
With $K$ possible symbols,
it estimates

$$
\Pr(X_t = b \mid X_{t-1} = a) = \frac{N(a, b) + 1}{N(a) + K},
$$

where $N(a, b)$ counts how often $a$ is followed by $b$ in a training text,
and $N(a)$ counts how often $a$ is followed by any symbol.
The added 1 in each count,
called add-one or Laplace smoothing [@jurafsky2026slp, section 3.6],
gives every pair a probability above 0,
including pairs the training text never shows.

:::
